analysis:
The supplied units are BASE-side excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 798-1637). The patch excerpt is truncated and shows head changes only to documentation: the scheduler configuration table (base lines 1087-1088; head 1087-1090) now documents wider prefill geometry. GPT-OSS, dense Qwen3.5/3.8 and Gemma 4 move from 512/2048 to 2048/4096 prefill chunk and step tokens. It also documents a bidirectionalMediaPrefillChunkCeiling of 512 and a changed solo-stripe policy. Other head ranges (1100-1146 and 2028-2041) are not visible in the supplied units, so I could not assess them.

These are documentation edits describing code behavior changes (EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift prefillGeometry). The implementation is not supplied. I found no change to authorization, attestation, encryption or key handling, and none to the prefix-cache storage that T-041 covers. The base text shows the prefix cache is unchanged: the SSD cache is keyed by cacheSalt and the sampler is not part of cache identity. The wider prefill chunks have possible availability effects, such as longer holds of the process-wide MLX evalLock during SSD staging or prefill, or memory pressure (T-010, T-029). The base text says the SSD staging import never evaluates or fences destinations, which limits that concern. The deadline admission and KV reservation controls described in the supplied text remain in place. Nothing visible shows these controls weakened.

Open question for integration: confirm that the code changes behind the doc table (prefillGeometry, usesWidePrefillChunk and the bidirectional media ceiling) preserve the memory-validated scheduler projection, KV reservation and first-token deadline admission at the larger chunk sizes. Also confirm that mixed-step prefill caps apply consistently. I report no security finding from this documentation-only evidence.
